working: Sum of coefficients = value at all variables 1. LHS: \((\alpha - 2 + 1)^{35} = (\alpha-1)^{35}\); RHS: \((1-\alpha)^{35}\). Since 35 is odd, \((\alpha-1)^{35} = -(1-\alpha)^{35}\), so the equality forces \(2(1-\alpha)^{35}=0\), i.e. \(\alpha=1\). Check \(\alpha=1\): \((x^2-2x+1)^{35}=(x-1)^{70}\) has coefficient sum 0, and \((x-y)^{35}\) also sums to 0.

working: If the 7 is the leading digit, the other four digits are any of the 9 non-7 digits: \(9^4\). If the 7 sits in one of the other 4 places, the leading digit has 8 choices (non-zero, non-7) and the remaining three have 9 each: \(4 \cdot 8 \cdot 9^3 = 32 \cdot 9^3\). Total \(9^4 + 32\cdot 9^3 = 41\cdot 9^3 = 29889\), confirmed by brute-force enumeration of all 5-digit numbers.

working: For a genuine quadratic need \(p^2-1>0\) and \(\Delta<0\): \(4(p-1)^2-8(p^2-1)=4(p-1)[(p-1)-2(p+1)]=-4(p-1)(p+3)<0 \Rightarrow (p-1)(p+3)>0 \Rightarrow p>1\) or \(p<-3\). The degenerate case \(p=1\) leaves the constant 2 > 0, so \(p=1\) is admissible; \(p=-1\) leaves \(-4x+2\), which is not always positive. \(p=-3\) gives \(2(2x-1)^2\), zero at \(x=1/2\), so excluded. Net set: \(p<-3\) or \(p\ge1\). Numerically confirmed at \(p=-4,-3,-1,1,1.5\).

working: Expanding gives \(3x^2-2(a+b+c)x+(ab+bc+ca)=0\), whose discriminant is \(4[(a+b+c)^2-3(ab+bc+ca)] = 4[a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca] = 2[(a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2] \ge 0\). So the roots are always real (not necessarily positive or negative — e.g. \(a=b=c=-1\) gives both roots \(-1\), and \(a=b=c=1\) gives both \(+1\), which rules out A and B).
